title: 2017 HMMT February Team Problem 6
statement: Let \(r\) be a positive integer. Show that if a graph \(G\) has no cycles of length at most \(2 r\), then it has at most \(|V|^{2016}\) cycles of length exactly \(2016 r\), where \(|V|\) denotes the number of vertices in the graph \(G\).

solutions.text: The key idea is that there is at most 1 path of length \(r\) between any pair of vertices, or else you get a cycle of length \(\leq 2 r\). Now, start at any vertex ( \(|V|\) choices) and walk 2015 times. There's at most \(|V|^{2016}\) ways to do this by the previous argument. Now you have to go from the end to the start, and there's only one way to do this. So we're done.
